children: Japan's import prices are expected to remain high as tensions in the Middle East drive up energy prices and alternative procurement costs, says Mizuho Securities economist Shota Amano. As a result, total import values are likely to maintain an upward trend, he says. "If the Iran situation settles and supply constraints ease, an increase in import volumes--primarily of Middle Eastern crude to replenish released oil reserves--is expected to boost overall import values," he adds. Imports rose 28.0% in August from a year earlier, following July's 27.9% growth, government data showed Wednesday.(megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
